thread:
liam: kicking off thread for the v3-int4 canary telemetry. pushed 1% traffic at 08:10 UTC. initial smoke looked fine for latency but we saw some weird long-doc MRR drift on the docs cohort.
priya: saw the same. 95p latency down ~35% which is great. overall tokens/sec up. but MRR vs baseline is -6% on long-doc slice (>=2k tokens).
esther: hallucination rate (auto-eval) is +2.8% absolute on the same slice, flagged by the evaluator. overall hallucination baseline 3.1% -> 5.9%.
liam: ugh. is that sustained across samples or just a tail?
priya: sample-level: looks concentrated in the long, multi-source citation prompts. quick diff shows the quant model drops some grounding tokens. small examples attached in the eval bucket.
deploy-bot: [canary report] v3-int4 canary@1%: latency P95 -35%, median -40%, MRR (global) -1.2%, MRR (long-doc slice) -6.0%, hallucination +2.8% abs. logs: s3://redwood-evals/1700009999/v3-int4/report.html
samir: heuristically sounds like kv-cache truncation or an attention kernel mismatch after quant. have we checked kv-warmup for long contexts?
liam: we did a kv warmup run but it was short. will re-run a warmup with longer seqs.
priya: also we should decide gating action. current auto-fallback policy in prod is: MRR drop >=5% (slice) OR hallucination increase >=2% abs -> trigger rollback. but that was calibrated mostly for shortdocs.
esther: recommendation: for long-doc slice we probably want a stricter hallucination watcher but longer observation window (30m sustained) to avoid noisy spikes. propose: keep MRR >=5% as immediate stop, but set hallucination auto-fallback to 2.5% abs sustained for 30 mins on any critical slice.
liam: agree on thresholds but can we limit auto-fallback to traffic >=5%? don't want 1% canaries auto-rollback too early.
priya: good point. for canaries <2% we prefer manual triage unless MRR drop >=10%. set policy: if traffic <2% then no auto-fallback for hallucination, only alert. if traffic >=2% then auto-fallback rules apply.
eng-oncall: @eng-oncall acknowledged. we'll need to route alerts to pager if MRR drop >=7% or if hallucination >4% abs. current pager thresholds?
samir: pager only for critical perf regressions. update suggestion: pager on MRR drop >=7% global or hallucination >4% abs sustained 15m. others just slack alerts.
liam: ok can we codify this quickly so rollout can continue but gated? runbook patch: set canary traffic to 0.5% -> monitor 60m with relaxed auto-fallback (manual for hallucination), then if stable promote to 2% and enable auto-fallback thresholds (MRR >=5% slice immediate rollback, hallucination >=2.5% sustained 30m).
priya: config snippet I will apply: 
```
rwctl rollout create --model redwood/v3-int4 --traffic 0.5% --observe 60m --auto-fallback "enabled=false" --notes "canary warmup long-doc focus"
```
liam: +1. also adding a specific slice watch: 
```
rwctl watch add --slice long-doc --metrics MRR,hallucination --window 60m --sustain 30m
```
esther: I'll start longer kv-warmup jobs and run sample generation diff against baseline v3fp16 for the long-doc cohort. will paste failures here.
deploy-bot: [action] rollout created by priya: id rlt-1700009999. canary traffic 0.5% observe=60m. auto-fallback disabled for hallucination for this step.
liam: tagging @samir to triage kernel/kv suspects. if warmup doesn't resolve, we'll consider increasing quant calibration (symmetric->asymmetric) or switching to int6 for long contexts.
samir: on it. will try the warmup + kernel trace. ETA 2-3 hours.
eng-oncall: noted. if any pager thresholds hit I'll start incident channel and follow the runbook. otherwise we'll reconvene after the 60m window. :thumbsup:
liam: thanks everyone. keep replies short — post only new data or decision changes. will reconvene at 09:15 UTC unless earlier rollback triggers.
